title.rendered: You Are My Friends: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “No longer do I call you servants… I have called you friends.” A morning devotional on the astonishing name Jesus gives to those who follow Him.

content.rendered:
In the upper room on the night before the cross, Jesus reached across a two-thousand-year religious tradition and reclassified His disciples. They had come into the room as servants of a rabbi. He was about to send them out as something no rabbi had ever called anyone. Friends.

The Gospel For Today | Friday, September 18, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“No longer do I call you servants, for a servant does not know what his master is doing; but I have called you friends, for all things that I heard from My Father I have made known to you.”
John 15:15 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

In the upper room, on the night before the cross, Jesus did something no rabbi in the history of Israel had ever done. He reached across a two-thousand-year religious tradition and reclassified the relationship between Himself and His followers. The disciples had come into the room, as they had come into every room for the previous three years, as students of a rabbi. Servants. Learners. Followers. That was the accepted category. In first-century Judea, a rabbi and his talmidim were teacher and servants. The rabbi taught. The servants learned. The rabbi commanded. The servants obeyed. There was affection in the relationship, but it was structured and unambiguous. And then, in the middle of His final teaching, Jesus said something that upended the whole structure. “No longer do I call you servants, for a servant does not know what his master is doing; but I have called you friends, for all things that I heard from My Father I have made known to you.”

Friends. The Greek word Jesus uses is philos. It is not a mild word. It is not the casual English “friend” that gets applied to acquaintances on social media. Philos is the intimate, personal, mutual, chosen relationship of shared life. It is the word for someone with whom you have no need to hide, no need to perform, no need to hold back. Jesus is telling the disciples that the relationship they are entering, on the far side of the cross, is not the relationship of employees to a boss. It is the relationship of intimate friends who share the same heart, the same mission, the same access to the Father.

He gives the reason in the same breath. “For a servant does not know what his master is doing.” The distinguishing mark of servanthood is that the servant carries out the master’s business without necessarily knowing why. The servant is on a need-to-know basis. Jesus is saying His disciples are no longer on a need-to-know basis. He has told them everything the Father has told Him. He has held nothing back. They know the plan. They know the heart of God behind the plan. They are inside the confidence of the Father, not outside looking in. That is what makes them friends and not merely servants.

The Passion Translation renders the transition with striking depth: “I have never called you ‘servants,’ because a master doesn’t confide in his servants, and servants don’t always understand what the master is doing. But I call you my most intimate friends, for I reveal to you everything that I’ve heard from my Father” (John 15:15 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “I do not call you servants (slaves) any longer, for the servant does not know what his master is doing (working out). But I have called you My friends, because I have made known to you everything that I have heard from My Father” (John 15:15 AMPC). Made known. Everything. Nothing withheld. That is what Jesus offered the eleven men in the upper room, and by extension, every believer since.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this is the identity Jesus places on you. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, you are not merely a servant of Christ, though servanthood is a real and honourable part of the Christian life. You are, in the New Testament vocabulary, His friend. Intimate. Trusted. Confided in. Included in the plan. Nothing withheld. And that changes how you pray. It changes how you serve. It changes how you read the Bible. It changes how you sit in His presence in the morning. The Master has become the Friend, and the Friend is inviting you in.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that Jesus has called me His friend. Not merely His servant. His friend. Intimate, trusted, included in the plan. Everything He has heard from You, He has made known to me. Today I come into Your presence with the confidence of a friend, not the distance of an employee. I refuse to relate to Jesus as if He is holding back. He has held nothing back. And I hold nothing back from Him. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Jesus has called me His friend. Not merely His servant. I am intimate, trusted, and included in the plan. Nothing is withheld between us today.
